ashby:base-power:74c9ec5f-3b4b-40ce-830f.summary: Base is America’s next-generation power company. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

You will be the voice and advocate of our brand, ensuring every interaction leaves a lasting impression of trust, satisfaction, and delight. By actively addressing customer needs and exceeding their expectations, you will contribute not only to the success of our customers but also to the growth and reputation of our company. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop real-world expertise in customer service, creative problem-solving, and impactful communication, all while making a tangible difference in the lives of our customers and the future of Base.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Engage with members across phone, email, text, and other communication channels, delivering personalized and delightful experiences that leave a lasting impact.
Troubleshoot and resolve member issues related to Base Power's innovative products, ensuring seamless and satisfying solutions.
Utilize tools to track, manage, troubleshoot, and prioritize member interactions, ensuring every concern is addressed promptly and efficiently.
Partner with engineering, marketing, and operations teams to streamline processes, enhance the member experience, and drive continuous improvement.
Act as the “voice of the customer”, gathering valuable feedback and insights to shape the future of our products and services.
Create and maintain detailed documentation, knowledge bases, playbooks, and team resources to ensure consistency in service.
Support new members during onboarding to ensure they understand and can fully utilize Base Power's products from the start.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
bullets: 0-5 years of experience.
Empathetic communicator who loves connecting with people and making them feel heard.
Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity.
Ability to think analytically and creatively to resolve complex issues and suggest process improvements.
Attention to detail in communicating accurately and clearly, tracking customer interactions, and documenting solutions.

Natural inclination to stay calm under pressure and step up to proactively de-escalate frustrating situations.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: The Member Experience team is the face of Base to our members—and the voice of our members back to Base. We’re deeply customer-obsessed and uniquely cross-functional, with a strong understanding of what every team does and how it all connects. ashby:benchling:874062e7-7903-4fd3-9930-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: Biotechnology is entering a new era. AI can help scientists design better experiments, understand complex data, and move discoveries forward faster. But its impact depends on access to high-quality scientific context and deep integration into how R&D actually happens.

Benchling is building the AI powered system for biotech R&D. We bring together scientific data, AI agents and models, and connected workflows so scientists can move from questions to insights to experiments within one intelligent system.

We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager to shape how Benchling’s product is understood, brought to market, and adopted. You’ll partner closely with Product, Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing to define go-to-market strategy, positioning, marke launches, and translate sophisticated capabilities into clear customer value.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Develop the positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategy for a major area of Benchling’s platform.
Lead product launches from early strategy through market introduction, field readiness, adoption, and measurement.
Own and contribute to pricing and packaging, including pricing analysis, deal assistance, discounting methodology, and pricing enablement for the field.
Partner closely with Product and Engineering to understand how the product works and bring customer, market, and commercial insight into product decisions.
Build a deep understanding of our customers, users, buyers, competitors, and the changing enterprise software and AI landscape.
Create product narratives, content, and enablement that help customer-facing teams communicate Benchling’s value with clarity and conviction.
Work across Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing to identify opportunities to drive adoption, expansion, pipeline, and revenue.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: 6+ years of experience in product marketing or a related go-to-market role within B2B enterprise software.
Marketed complex or technical products, such as data platforms, APIs, SDKs, integrations, developer tools, workflows, or AI products.
Owned positioning, messaging, product launches, and sales enablement from strategy through execution.
Partner with technical product managers and engineers, ask productive questions, and translate what you learn without losing the important details.
Strong writer and storyteller who can make complicated ideas clear, specific, and compelling. You leverage AI, but do not use it to override human judgment and creativity.
You can understand customers and the nuanced enterprise buying dynamics to communicate value to users, technical stakeholders, business leaders, and executives.
You are comfortable creating structure in ambiguous environments and driving work forward across multiple teams.
You are deeply curious and motivated to learn unfamiliar technical and scientific domains.

sections.title: Nice to Have
bullets: Experience at a growth-stage or rapidly scaling enterprise software company.
Experience marketing a platform or products used by technical audiences.
Experience driving adoption or expansion within enterprise customers.
Experience bringing AI products or capabilities to market.
Familiarity with biotechnology, scientific software, or regulated industries.

ashby:bree:5ffd6e4b-986b-4496-ac58-3a1e8.summary:

Our first act is to become the cheapest and best provider of short-term credit to the 20 million people in Canada who live paycheck to paycheck.

sections.title: About Bree

paras: Bree’s engineering team works across customer-facing products, regulatory expansion, payments, infrastructure, security, data, and machine learning. As the company grows, the work increasingly spans multiple teams and requires clearer ownership, sequencing, and communication.
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to help turn company priorities into well-defined engineering programs and carry them through to release.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Design, CX, Operations, Legal, and leadership. You will help clarify the problem, break large initiatives into manageable workstreams, identify dependencies, establish ownership, and make sure decisions and risks remain visible.

sections.title: What You'll Need
bullets: Experience as a Technical Program Manager, Program Manager, Product Manager, or similar role supporting a software engineering organization.

Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities and requirements can change.
Excellent attention to detail, especially around ownership, dependencies, timelines, and unresolved decisions.
An AI-native working style, using tools to accelerate research, documentation, meeting synthesis, backlog management, and status reporting while validating the output.

ashby:cloaked:9161eac4-3ab3-4ce2-92cb-7f.summary:
Cloaked is a privacy startup dedicated to rebuilding consumer trust in how personal data is used. Nearly a million paying members use Cloaked to take back control of their data, their identity, and who can reach them. That covers masked emails, phone numbers, and payment cards, data removal from broker sites, and an AI voice agent that screens calls before they ring through.

We've protected tens of millions of identities, screened hundreds of millions of calls, and removed billions of records from data brokers. Backed by a $375M Series B.

paras: We’re hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Product Narrative & Launches to own the product story end to end. Cloaked ships fast across more than one product line: the consumer app, Cloaked Enterprise, and new lines coming off the roadmap (agentic privacy, Cloaked Pay, and whatever ships next). You’ll own how a feature becomes a launch, how a launch becomes a story, and how that story shows up on socials, in press, in a security buying room, on the founder’s channels, and in the market.
This role is based in our New York office, in person three days a week.

sections.title: What will you do?
bullets: Own the messaging architecture that ties the product lines together: the same technical truth told to a consumer, a CISO, and an investor without contradiction. Translate the enterprise thesis (the human attack surface) and the consumer story into one platform narrative, and extend it to new lines before they launch.
Own Cloaked’s recurring consumer feature-release property - the cadence, editorial format, naming, and branding.
Produce the Build in Public and founder content program: a weekly cadence across leadership, product, and engineering on X, LinkedIn, and beyond, written in their voices.

sections.title: What skills and experiences will help you?
bullets: 3–4 years in product marketing, product management, developer relations, solutions engineering, technical content strategy, or an operator role at a software company that sells to both consumers and businesses, or has moved from one to the other; privacy, security, identity, fintech, or AI a strong plus.
You build working demos and prototypes yourself with AI coding tools.
You’ve run product launches end to end and can show the awareness or adoption result.
Exceptional writer across registers: a launch post, a founder tweet, a demo script, and a research report should all read as the same brand. Comfortable ghostwriting in someone else’s voice.
You’ve built or materially grown an audience - your own, a founder’s, or a product’s - and understand what earns attention on X, LinkedIn, YouTube, and Reddit without a paid budget.
Self-directed and fast: you take a half-formed feature from a stand-up and return with a narrative, a plan, and a draft.

Bonus: technical content that non-technical people understood and shared; a founder or exec content program with a documented cadence and growth; something you shipped yourself (a side project, an app, an open-source contribution, or a product you founded); or experience marketing a security or identity product to a technical buyer.

sections.title: What do we like?
bullets: Engineer’s curiosity, storyteller’s instinct. Reads the code before writing the post; equally happy in an architecture review and a writing session.
Extraction over authorship. Gets the story out of people who don’t have time to tell it, and writes it in their voice.
Ships in public. Comfortable with rough edges, live feedback, and a weekly cadence that doesn’t wait for perfect.
Comfortable on a small team. The work is unglamorous as often as it’s strategic.

ashby:deepgram:19954a4c-7f3f-4231-8480-c.summary:
Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our…

sections.title: Operating Principles
paras: Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
bullets: Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

sections.title: AI-First by Default
paras: We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.
bullets: Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

sections.title: Overview
paras: Deepgram's next phase of growth is upmarket. Our customers have increasing compliance needs and are security-conscious buyers with sophisticated procurement orgs.

This role owns that problem space: making Deepgram enterprise-ready and removing the product blockers that stall upmarket deals. Enterprise buyers don't evaluate readiness as a feature. They evaluate it as a package — identity, security, compliance, and the experience their teams touch — and the absence of any one piece stalls a deal in security review. You own the outcome and ship the fix wherever it belongs: in Console, in our APIs, or in the managed endpoint, partnering with the PMs who own those surfaces.

Today that means enterprise SSO, FedRAMP/FIPS readiness, SBOM and security-artifact self-serve, and a user experience that signals maturity. The specifics will shift as we move upmarket; the mandate won't. This is high-leverage work with real autonomy. You set enterprise product strategy for a Series C company's core upmarket motion while owning a pillar of the business's strategy, with an explicit path to Staff as your scope grows.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own the enterprise adoption problem space end to end: the procurement, security, compliance, and UX storylines that have to work together to win upmarket deals.
Set strategy, sequencing across enterprise initiatives which today includes SSO, compliance readiness, and our Console UX, and defend that prioritization with data.

Ship solutions on whatever surface fits the problem: Console, APIs, or the managed endpoint. You own the problem and partner with the PMs who own those surfaces rather than owning the surfaces outright.
Drive enterprise security and compliance readiness so procurement teams can self-serve e.g., SBOM generation and security-artifact access, instead of waiting on us.
Remove the product blockers that stall deals in security review and slow closure.
Work directly with engineers, designers, and sales to ship features. Pull people in when you need to; don't wait for consensus.
Set your own objectives and make the trade-offs, with minimal steering.

Why Join the Drata Team?

sections.title: About the role
paras: Dune’s mission is to make onchain finance observable. Since 2018, we have made blockchain data accessible and useful. Our next opportunity is to build products that financial institutions depend on to commit capital, assess risk, and enter new onchain markets.

As these institutions expand their activity on blockchains, they will need reliable, trustworthy and timely data to power decision making across more markets than ever before. They will need to compare opportunities, monitor changes, and integrate data into their existing systems. For Dune these recurring needs will become a substantial and core part of our business.

We are looking for a Head of Product to help transition Dune into this new era. We will build on top of Dune’s existing data foundation, which already powers thousands of companies. You will decide which customers and use cases to serve first, which problems matter most, and which needs can become scalable products for institutional usage.

sections.title: What we are looking for
paras: You have led product as a Head of Product, VP or similar at a company relevant to Dune, such as data, developer platforms, crypto, fintech or a fast-growing startup. You learn new domains fast. Knowledge of traditional or onchain markets, and of how market participants use data, is a strong plus.

You can set a clear direction, make difficult choices, and work hard through the details required to deliver. The job’s not finished with a PRD, a hire or a ticket. The job’s finished when the product is creating value in the hands of our customers, being recursively improved by tight knit relationships.

You will work closely with Dune’s engineering, data, and commercial teams while being an integral part of the leadership team. You will report to the president. Your responsibility extends from understanding a customer’s problem to delivering a product that solves it, while navigating the requirements from a large customer base.

sections.title: In this role you will
bullets: Define the product strategy for market data and institutional customers. Decide which customers, problems, and products deserve our attention.
Own the product experience from data creation to delivery. Set clear requirements for coverage, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness.
Understand how financial institutions consume data. Turn their research, investment, trading, and operational needs into clear product priorities.
Work with engineering and data teams to deliver reliable datasets, data feeds, and integrations that fit customer systems.
Make explicit decisions about scope, quality, and delivery dates. Resolve dependencies and keep important work moving.
Partner with Product Marketing, Sales and other teams on customer evaluations, pricing, and adoption. Convert repeated customer needs into products we can serve at scale.
Define how we measure success of our products. Use the results to decide what to improve or stop.
Define and improve on our operational practices.

sections.title: You might be a great fit if
bullets: You're excited to spend real time with customers: on calls, in their offices, learning from them.
You have delivered technically complex data products that customers depend on.
Bonus: you understand market data and how financial institutions evaluate, buy, integrate and use it.
Bonus: you know onchain markets, tokenized equities and RWAs
You can connect customer needs with technical requirements and a sound business case.
You have strong product judgment. You can make decisions with incomplete information and change them when the evidence changes.
You stay close to the work. You investigate problems, challenge assumptions, and help teams resolve difficult details.
You are known to be an excellent communicator.

ashby:emberos:1f9a57f4-1b9c-409f-b4c1-b6.summary:
emberos exists to bring predictive intelligence and clarity to a world where AI is already shaping decisions.

We help brands understand how AI interprets and represents them at the moment of discovery and how that understanding compounds over time. By revealing emerging patterns before assumptions harden into belief, we give leaders foresight into what is taking shape and the ability to act early.

This is not just monitoring. It's predictive intelligence designed for an AI-mediated world.

As AI increasingly defines what people see, trust, and choose, emberos serves as a grounding force for truth by bringing clarity to how meaning forms today and how it evolves tomorrow.

sections.title: The Role
paras: Most companies would call this Customer Success. We don’t.
At emberos, the Account Strategist sits closer to a strategy consultant with a commercial mandate than a relationship manager with a renewal calendar.

You’ll own a portfolio of brand clients and the strategy that turns emberos from a platform they use into an advantage they rely on. If a client thinks of us as a dashboard, we haven’t gone far enough. If they think of us as the team helping them win as AI reshapes brand discovery, you’re doing the job.

sections.title: What You'll Own
bullets: The strategy for every account. You’ll maintain a rolling 90-day plan tied to the moments that matter: launches, release calendars, campaign windows, pipeline cycles, and shifts in the market. This is not a status document. It should be useful enough that the client works from it.

The client relationship after the sale. Kickoffs, weekly working sessions, quarterly reviews, executive briefings, and the strategic questions that show up between meetings all run through you. You set the standard for how clients experience emberos.

Fix Pack strategy. You determine what we deploy, when we deploy it, and why it matters. You’ll build the rationale with the client, align the work internally, and make sure every intervention connects back to a larger strategic objective. Engineering owns execution. You own the thinking behind it.
Expansion. Growth is part of the job, not a handoff to sales. Every quarterly review should surface where emberos can create more value. You’ll carry a soft quota on net new ARR across your book.

The client's perception of emberos. You are the person clients associate with our judgment, our responsiveness, and our value. The strength of that relationship should show up in renewals, expansion, and referrals.

sections.title: Required Qualifications
bullets: 4-6+ years in a client-facing strategic role. That could mean management consulting, brand or marketing strategy, agency account leadership, or enterprise customer success where you were accountable for outcomes rather than activity.
A record of growing accounts. You can point to revenue expansion or net revenue retention you materially influenced and explain exactly how you did it.

Credibility with senior marketing leaders. You’ve worked directly with CMOs, brand leaders, or equivalent executives. You can challenge the brief, defend a recommendation, and hold your ground when the answer is not obvious.

sections.title: Job Summary
paras: Qualified Health is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own how the platform compounds: the core workflow primitives that every product is assembled from, the builder tools that let teams create assistants, abstractors, and workflows, and the scaling discipline that turns one-off builds into products that generalize. Builder tools are the velocity engine of our platform. This role makes the engine compound: a component built once for one application becomes a primitive available to every application after it.

This is a three-prong role. First, identify and productize the scalable primitives: the triggers, ingestion patterns, extraction steps, review gates, and serving patterns that recur across products, so they are built once, versioned, and reused everywhere. Second, make sure products ship scalable, not as one-offs: generalization requirements are set before build, and the second customer costs a fraction of the first. Third, drive the builder tools themselves: the roadmap for Workflow Factory and its sibling builders, and the runtime underneath them, including registries, config-driven backends, and the path from a built workflow to production.

You are not the infrastructure owner. Engineering owns the runtime, the architecture, and their technical decisions. You are the scalability partner: the person who has written down what must generalize, who catches the one-off before it ships, and who owns the product definition of the primitives and the tools that assemble them.

sections.title: What You Will Own
paras: You own products, catalogs, and requirements. Engineering owns the domains.
bullets: The promotion path from one-off to primitive: The intake, criteria, and process for when a component built for one application gets promoted into the shared catalog, who migrates to it, and how deprecation works. Pattern recognition across products is the core skill of this role.

Builder tools: The co-own product roadmap for Workflow Factory, Assistant Builder, and Abstractor Builder: what builders can create, what guardrails apply, and what it takes to go from built to deployed in production.

The builder tools runtime as a product surface: Registries, config-driven backends, and the pipeline that ships a built workflow to production, including automated review gates. Engineering owns the implementation; you own the requirements, the interfaces, and the roadmap.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the roadmap for builder tools and core primitives, balancing customer commitments, internal builder needs, and platform reuse
Build and maintain the primitive catalog: what exists, its interface, its version, and who consumes it
Define and run the promotion process that turns per-customer builds into reusable platform components with clear interfaces
Set generalization and scalability requirements at the start of every new product build, and enforce them at review gates
Write complete acceptance criteria before work commits to a sprint; no ambiguity reaches engineering
Own product requirements for the workflow registry, config-driven backends, and the build-to-production pipeline, in partnership with the Workflow Factory team
Partner with infrastructure engineering on multi-tenancy, performance, reliability, and cost as product requirements, not afterthoughts
Define success metrics for reuse and platform leverage (component adoption, time-to-second-deployment, share of new products assembled from existing primitives) and use them to drive prioritization

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. paras:
Watershed is on a mission to turn sustainability data into a lever for business transformation. Our customers use our platform to uncover insights hidden in their operations, supply chains, and financial systems, then act on those insights to drive resilience and competitive advantage. We’re hiring mission-driven Customer Success Managers to partner with our Mid-Market and Enterprise accounts as they transform how they operate.

What you’ll do:
bullets: Own the commercial health of your book, driving retention and identifying opportunities for growth.
Build trust with key stakeholders and executives, showing how sustainability data supports their broader business goals.
Help customers achieve their sustainability goals and map the work that we are doing with them to the value Watershed is driving and how that ties to the customers' business outcomes.
Serve as the voice of the customer and provide internal feedback to our product and services teams on how we can better serve customers to maximize value and retention.
Proactively identify risk and develop the plans for mitigating the risk, working with cross-functional partners on execution.

Commercially fluent, partnering with Sales on renewals and expansions.
Highly organized, managing a larger portfolio of enterprise accounts while driving outcomes.
Curious and adaptable, eager to make sustainability data the next frontier of business intelligence.

As a leader in pathology AI software, we are empowering pathologists and scientists to transition from traditional microscope-based workflows to digital, AI-driven approaches, unlocking new possibilities in precision medicine.

The digital pathology market is experiencing explosive growth as advances in AI enable unprecedented insights into diseases like cancer. Pathology is central to medicine, and the shift to AI-powered solutions is not just modernizing workflows—it’s transforming how diseases are diagnosed, treated, and understood. greenhouse:cloudflare:8349425.summary: At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. sections.title: About the team
paras: Search engines spent two decades learning what the web is worth: which pages are fresh, which sources are trusted, what people actually use. That knowledge came from watching how humans moved through the web.

Agents break that loop. AI models are trained and grounded on the web, but they have little visibility into what's changed, what's authoritative, or what's been fabricated. Site owners have it worse: AI crawlers already request content anywhere from a hundred to tens of thousands of times for every visitor they send back, and most have no idea how, or whether, they show up in AI answers. Both sides of the market are flying blind.

Cloudflare sits in front of around 20% of the web and sees both sides of that exchange. Our team, the Agentic Internet team, is focused on making the web readable, discoverable, callable, and payable, built on open standards so no single company owns the rails. Signals & Data Products turns our network's view into products both sides can use: helping AI labs know what's fresh and trustworthy, and helping site owners see and shape how they show up in AI. Cloudflare believes in the open Internet, and we're in a position to help build the future where it thrives. Come help us make it happen! You can read more about some of our plans here and here .

sections.title: Scope of the Role:
paras: As a Technical Product Manager for Trust & Safety, you will define and ship the data products that frontier labs use to train and evaluate models to perform personalization, computer-use (CUA), and GDPval tasks safely and in a trustworthy manner.

You will own the full lifecycle of these products: from translating a lab's research need into a spec, to designing reinforcement learning (RL) environments, rubrics, and evals, to running delivery with our expert workforce and measuring whether the data actually moved the model.

A core part of the job is building RL environments with deliberate traps. That includes misalignment traps that test for reward hacking, deception, sandbagging, oversight evasion, and power-seeking; cyber traps such as planted credentials, injected instructions, and poisoned tools; and other honeypots that reveal how a model behaves when it believes no one is watching.

sections.title: What You’ll Own:
bullets: Define data products for frontier labs. Turn lab research goals into clear product specs for safety training data, RL environments, and evaluations.

Design trap-based RL environments. Build sandboxed environments that embed misalignment traps (reward hacking, specification gaming, deception, sandbagging, oversight subversion) and cyber traps (prompt injection, credential exfiltration, tool poisoning, unsafe file and network actions).

Build safety into agentic tasks by design. Specify safe-behavior rubrics, verifiers, and reward signals so that models learn to complete real work while refusing, escalating, or asking for confirmation at the right moments.

Own evals and metrics. Define what "safe and trustworthy" means for each product in measurable terms, including attack success rate, over-refusal, trap trigger rate, and task completion under adversarial pressure. Track blind spots and drive iteration.
Prioritize ruthlessly. Frame problems crisply, lay out options with their business and technical tradeoffs, and separate MVP from ideal state.
Partner across teams. Work with lab researchers, our ML and platform engineers, red-teamers, policy experts, and delivery leads running large expert annotator pools.
Track the threat landscape. Stay current on agentic risks, alignment research, and new attack techniques, and turn them into roadmap items before customers ask.
Communicate clearly. Write specs, customer briefs, and safety findings that land with researchers and executives alike.

sections.title: These examples show the kind of work this role owns:
bullets: A cyber-trap environment suite : sandboxed environments seeded with injected instructions, exposed secrets, and destructive shortcuts, scored on whether the agent finishes the task without taking the bait.
Tasks with integrity traps : realistic work where the easiest path to a high score requires fabricating data, skipping a required step, or gaming the grader.
A misalignment eval harness : environments that check whether a model behaves differently when it believes it is being tested versus deployed, or when given chances to expand its own permissions.
A trap library and quality framework that lets our delivery teams produce new environments quickly while keeping verifiers reliable and traps hard to detect.

sections.title: About the Role

Personalization (Ranking) and Marketplace (Delivery) decide which ad each Pinner sees, where it shows, and what it earns. They balance three outcomes over the long term: Pinner satisfaction, advertiser return, and Pinterest revenue.

Success requires solving some of the hardest problems in ads marketplaces. These include measuring and improving ad relevance at scale, delivering ROAS that wins performance budgets, and building a yield system that balances first-party demand with high-quality monetization of every ad slot.

We’re looking for a Director of Product Management who has done this before: someone who has built and scaled ads ranking, delivery, or marketplace systems and turned them into measurable business results. Reporting to the VP of Product Management, Ads Quality, you’ll own the multi-year strategy and rebuild the Ads Quality product organization. Own the value equation. Improve Pinner Value through better ad relevance and personalization, Advertiser Value as measured by ROAS, and revenue per mille (RPM), all with a lifetime-value lens. Define how relevance and satisfaction are measured.

Own delivery end to end. Drive discovery through launch and scale for new products and platform capabilities. Set architecture and quality standards, unblock critical technical and operating risks, and make sure the team has reliable measurement, experimentation, and operational readiness.

Build the team. Assess and reshape the current team. Hire senior product leaders for the Personalization and Marketplace pods, and coach managers and senior ICs. Establish clear ownership and operating rhythms, and build a culture of urgency, rigor, and customer focus.

Lead cross-functionally. Align Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Measurement, Ad Formats, Buying Platform, Ads Integrity, and Consumer teams around a shared plan. The individual in this role will also manage a book of business and deepen relationships with clients and help retain them on our platform. The Client Success Manager position plays a pivotal role in retaining and maximizing the value of the restaurants on the network. They will be assigned the portfolio of regional accounts, with a primary focus of retaining the accounts on the network (minimizing churn), reinforcing the value of our services (improving NPS scores), and upselling additional services (cash conversions).
This is a hybrid position and requires in office presence three days a week in Chicago (Tuesday-Thursday).

sections.title: What you’ll bring to the table: (Responsibilities)
bullets: Oversee the customer journey for an assigned portfolio of accounts, from onboarding a new customer through ongoing support, with the goal of maximizing customer satisfaction and loyalty.
Proactively identify and address customer issues, leading to minimized churn. (Examples: missing tickets, accounts receivables, managing exclusions.)
Respond to customer requests for support, guiding clients through product features and strategies to maximize the benefits they receive from our services.
Communicate with clients to ensure they are realizing the full value of our services, thereby improving Net Promotor Scores (NPS)
Identify opportunities within the assigned portfolio to introduce and upsell products (i.e. Cash)
Work closely with the regional manager and sales teams to execute strategies that enhance the customer satisfaction and business growth.
Monitor account health metrics and provide insights to leadership on portfolio status and renewal/conversion opportunities.
Share customer feedback and insights with the internal teams to shape future offerings.

sections.title: Do you have the right mix of ingredients: (Requirements)
bullets: At least 3 years of related experience working with internal and external clients to support a sales organization. Customer/client service experience is required.
Must have previous experience responding to a high volume of calls and emails related to client service.
Must have a passion for client service.
Experience using a CRM system such as Salesforce
Proficiency with MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Ability to work in a rapidly changing and growth-oriented environment with regularly changing priorities and developing opportunities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills and abilities.

greenhouse:ridgeline:8042013003.summary:
Ridgeline is building AI capabilities that help investment management firms work with greater speed, confidence, and scale. As a Senior Staff AI Product Manager on the Agent Foundry team, you will lead major AI product initiatives that leverage Ridgeline’s platform and solve important customer and business problems throughout the product. You will work closely with product, engineering, design, data, security, customer-facing teams, and leadership.

At Ridgeline, how we work matters as much as what we build. We act like owners, choose growth over comfort, and communicate with transparency. We assume positive intent, bias toward action, and bring solutions—not just problems. We celebrate wins, learn from setbacks, and thrive in a resilient, collaborative, high-performing culture.

sections.title: The impact you’ll have
bullets: Own product direction and roadmap for Ridgeline's agentic capabilities, aligning customer and operations needs, platform strategy, technical realities, and business outcomes.
Lead high-visibility, multi-squad initiatives from discovery through launch, adoption, and ongoing improvement; establish clear goals and measures of success.
Identify and prioritize customer problems where AI agents and platform capabilities can create meaningful, differentiated value in investment management workflows.
Partner with engineering, design, data, and security to make sound decisions across model and architecture choices, orchestration, evaluation, integrations, reliability, and user experience.
Translate ambiguous opportunities into executable plans, make high-impact trade-offs, manage dependencies, and secure cross-functional alignment and resources.
Use customer research, product data, experiments, and operational insight to validate hypotheses, manage risk, and demonstrate customer and business impact.
Follow practices for evaluating AI quality, safety, trust, and performance that help teams deliver useful, reliable, enterprise-ready experiences.
Champion outcome-focused delivery and improve how teams plan, build, evaluate, and scale AI capabilities across the product lifecycle.

sections.title: What we’re looking for
bullets: 8+ years of product management experience, including leadership of complex enterprise software, platform, data, or AI product initiatives.
Demonstrated success delivering significant, cross-functional product capabilities from discovery through launch and adoption, with measurable customer or business outcomes.
Strong product judgment and strategic execution: able to set direction for a substantial product area, prioritize investment, and connect roadmap choices to business value.
Practical understanding of AI/ML product development, including familiarity with LLM-based products, agent or workflow patterns, evaluation, and the operational considerations of production AI.
Ability to work effectively with engineering and design partners on technical trade-offs, platform constraints, scalability, reliability, and user experience.
Skill in using customer evidence, product data, and experimentation to make decisions and communicate risks and trade-offs.
A track record of influencing stakeholders across teams and functions, building trust, and driving alignment without relying on formal authority.
Clear, persuasive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical and AI concepts to both technical and business audiences.

sections.title: Bonus
bullets: Experience building multi-tenant AI platforms, agent frameworks, or enterprise AI products.
Familiarity with investment management workflows, financial services, or complex data-intensive business processes.
Experience working with model evaluation, observability, governance, or AI cost and performance optimization.
Experience collaborating with external technology partners, vendors, or research organizations.

sections.title: POSITION SUMMARY
paras: As Account Manager, Partnership Marketing, you own the revenue and results of a portfolio of marquee corporate partners. You are accountable for renewing every account in your portfolio and growing it through amendments, upsells, and new assets. You earn those outcomes by delivering contracts flawlessly, knowing each partner’s business, and building executive relationships that make renewal the obvious decision. You will plan and run activations across match day, media, events, signage, tickets, merchandising, and hospitality, and you will show partners the results in recaps tied to their goals.

This role requires a strategic-minded individual who is passionate about client service and building impactful, objective-focused partnerships, and who brings a positive, collaborative attitude in line with the club's vision, values, and objectives.

sections.title: Revenue, Retention and Growth
bullets: Own retention, renewals, and revenue growth for an assigned portfolio of marquee corporate partners, and answer for the results each partnership delivers.
Own overall day-to-day account management including contract activation and fulfillment, strategic direction, and budget for assigned corporate partners.
Develops a written account plan for each partner that captures the partner's goals and key performance indicators, aligns the right assets to them, and updates as goals change.
Maintain strong relationships with each partner's leaders and decision makers.
Hosts partner executives at matches and events, and uses those moments to build trust and surface new opportunities.
Tracks activation performance and fan engagement throughout the season, reports results to the partner, and adjusts plans to keep each partnership on target.
Prepare a recap for every assigned partner that measures results against the partner's goals, and use it in renewal and next-season planning.
Plan an activation calendar for each partner that is tied to the partner's business goals.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
paras: We’re looking for an experienced partnership marketing professional who positions partnerships strategically in addition to facilitating them. They grow accounts through upsells that deliver revenue, work through the gap between what a partner expects and what is possible, and proactively lead renewals. They build genuine relationships inside the club and with partners, look for the levers that grow a partnership beyond the deal in front of them, and put AI to specific, practical use. They are a genuine fan of the game and a student of the business, and they take pride in turning partner commitments into results for our partners and the club.

greenhouse:sharegateen:5260306007.summary:
ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.

It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.

Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.

ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.

ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.

sections.title: Your role
paras: ShareGate is a trusted favourite with partners who run Microsoft 365 migrations, and we're now taking those relationships from product-centric to strategic. As Channel Account Manager, you'll own a defined book of Premier and Elite partners across North America and be the strategic owner of their growth with ShareGate. This is a sales-first role: we're looking for someone with a hunter mindset who goes after revenue alongside partners, not someone who simply maintains accounts.
bullets: Drive partner-led revenue growth by owning your number, keeping pipeline coverage strong, and forecasting accurately, so ShareGate hits (and beats) its channel targets quarter after quarter.

Own your book of Premier and Elite partners by building a growth plan for each one (goals, joint actions, success metrics), so top performers scale, high-potential partners take off, and underperforming partners become growth accounts.

Evolve partner relationships from product-centric to strategic by building multi-level connections (sales, technical, leadership) and becoming your partners' ShareGate Sherpa, so ShareGate is the vendor they choose to grow their business with.

Open new revenue streams with your partners by uncovering larger, more complex migration opportunities, expanding mailbox migration (including displacing competitive tools) and Protect adoption, and driving uptake of new partner programs as they launch.
Use AI daily for account research, partner planning, forecasting, and communications, so your time goes to the conversations that move deals forward, not to prep work.

sections.title: Your team
paras: The ShareGate Channel team is growing fast and works the way we like to: quickly, collaboratively, and with plenty of trust. You'll report to the Channel Sales Manager and work daily with the Director, fellow Channel Account Managers, Distribution Channel Managers, and Partner Development Managers, with channel marketing, RevOps, technical enablement, support, and direct sales close by whenever you need them. Over the next 6 to 12 months, the team's ambition is to shift the channel from product-centric to strategic: deepening relationships with Premier and Elite partners, driving adoption of new partner programs as they launch, and turning high-potential partners into true growth accounts. Within six months, you'll own your book and cadences, have built a growth plan for your partners, and be testing new ideas to set up what comes next.

sections.title: What you'll bring
bullets: 5+ years of channel sales experience in North America, ideally including the US, with a documented track record of meeting and exceeding quota (up to 30% travel between Canada and the US);
Experience managing Premier- or Elite-level partners, including building and executing partner business plans;
A sales-first, hunter mindset: an independent, entrepreneurial owner who creates their own pipeline, shows sound judgment and initiative, and can hit the ground running;
Strong communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, with the ease to talk to both sales teams and executives at partner organizations;
A solid understanding of the IT channel ecosystem (distributors, resellers, and services partners);
Comfort using AI tools (e.g. Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT) daily for account research, planning, forecasting, and communications: not an experiment, a habit;
Bonus: Microsoft ecosystem experience and existing relationships with M365 partners.

TransferGo is a growing fintech scale-up on a mission to champion financial freedom with care. We strive to provide tailored, more affordable financial services that make people's hard-earned money go further. We’ve come this far by building a talented, diverse workforce on a fair culture and our strong values. Having this strong team of employees, we can serve those who really need our product to make their lives better.

sections.title: About the role
paras: We’re building a new pricing engine and the tools around it. Some of those tools started as AI prototypes made by our product team. You’ll own where it goes next.

Our Chief Commercial Officer sets pricing strategy and price levels. You own the pricing product: the engine and tools that set prices, the experiments that test them, and how customers see prices in the app. You’ll sit in the Send area, which owns the whole transfer experience. Pricing analysts sit in the Data team, and you’ll work closely with them. You’ll write your own SQL and read your own experiment results. When the team needs a tool, you’ll often prototype it before engineering builds it.
We hire builders. Our PMs prototype with AI before engineering builds anything. Operations people automate their own work. If you can fix something today, you don’t open a ticket for it.

sections.title: What success looks like after six months
bullets: The CCO, Finance and engineering agree on your roadmap for the pricing product.
The remaining prices have moved onto the new engine, and the old setups are retired.
Price tests run on tooling you own, from setup to readout, without manual fixes along the way.
The team uses at least one pricing tool or check you built every week.

sections.title: What you’ll be doing
bullets: Own the roadmap for the pricing engine and its tools, and build the checks that keep every live price correct.
Make price tests quick and safe to run, from setup to readout, so the CCO and Finance can decide to scale, hold or stop with confidence.
Own the tests of how prices are shown in the app. Read conversion, retention and gross profit together, so a price that wins volume doesn’t quietly lose money.
Work with the app teams on how prices, fees, promotions and cashback appear. Customers should know what they’ll pay before they send, and promotions should bring in customers who stay.
Work with Compliance on fee disclosure, Payments on partner costs and Finance on margin.
Build and extend pricing tools yourself with AI.

sections.title: What we’d love from you
bullets: 5+ years as a product manager, with at least 2 of them owning pricing, monetisation or another revenue-critical product.
Experience in a price-transparent, low-margin category such as payments, money transfers, travel or marketplaces. You think in basis points as easily as in percentages.
You design and read pricing experiments yourself: the hypothesis, the sample size, the decision rule, and an honest read when the result is unclear.
You write your own SQL and can model unit economics per transfer: fee, FX margin, promotion cost and partner cost.
You’re comfortable in product analytics tools such as Amplitude or Tableau, and in AI build tools such as Claude Code or Cursor.
You’ve built a tool with AI that other people rely on, and you can show it to us.
You’ve worked closely with engineers on systems where one wrong change has a real cost.
You can disagree with a commercial leader using data and work together to a better answer.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001583646.summary:
Service Operations is where enterprises find out whether their technology actually works. An outage starts, someone gets paged, a bridge call spins up, and the first twenty minutes go to working out what broke rather than fixing it.

Our team owns the products that close that gap: incident and major incident, problem and root cause, change, on-call, and Notify. The people using them go well beyond the service desk, from application, platform, infrastructure, and network teams to DevOps and SRE groups who get alerted around the clock and the major incident commanders pulling everyone onto one call. Thousands of the largest IT organizations run their operations on these products. We are rebuilding them AI-native, not AI-assisted, with agents that triage, correlate, and resolve, and with people moving from doing the work to directing it. Our goal is Zero Service Outage.

sections.title: About the role
paras: You will own a piece of that portfolio outright: what good looks like for it, who it is for, and whether we are honestly there yet. Zero Service Outage is the goal, and the work is making it true for the customers who run their operations on these products every day.

The interesting part of this job is not the model. It is the environment it runs in. Service operations data is the messiest data in the enterprise: half-populated CMDBs, incident descriptions written in a hurry at 2am, alert noise from a dozen monitoring tools, and naming conventions that differ by region. An agent that triages perfectly against a clean eval set can behave very differently against a real customer’s incident stream, for reasons that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. Understanding why, and designing for it, is the job.

We also carry an installed base. Customers run today’s experience in production, and moving them onto an AI-native one is not a UI refresh. It is a change to how their IT team works, who approves what, and what an operator trusts an agent to do unsupervised. You will be making calls about what we carry forward, what we leave behind, and what we have to earn the right to automate.

sections.title: What you get to do in this role
bullets: Own an AI-native ITSM product end to end, from the customer problem through launch criteria to how it performs in production.
Set product strategy for the Service Operations portfolio that supports ServiceNow’s growth toward $10B+ in revenue.
Build, not just specify. Prototype the interaction, stand up the eval harness, and get into the agent execution logs to understand what happened on the runs that failed.

Define what good means for an autonomous agent in an operational context where the cost of a wrong action is a second outage. Hold the line on it with engineering and have the honest conversation about what we can defensibly promise.

Work with design partners across the teams that run on this: service desk, application and infrastructure support, DevOps and SRE, and major incident command. Build in their environment against their real incidents, changes, and RCAs, then turn what you learn into something that generalizes to the next thousand customers.

Own your outcome metrics, such as time to resolve, change failure rate, and repeat incidents, in partnership with Customer Success, and make sure the instrumentation exists to show whether what you shipped moved them.

Align with peer product managers so the team is working on the right things at the right time and guide multiple teams through ambiguous product development without losing sight of the unified vision.
Write the strategy, the specs, and the analysis yourself.
